extracted.intended_audience: State, local, tribal, territorial, and Federal emergency managers; new or prospective Public Information Officers (PIOs); executive personnel who need PIO role knowledge
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and requirements for FEMA's introductory Public Information Officer (PIO) courses (IS-29 independent study and E0105 classroom) that establish awareness of the PIO role and foundational skills for full or part-time PIOs. Includes target audience, prerequisites, delivery modes, and time commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Awareness and Basics
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of the concepts underlying the PIO role, and a basic understanding of the PIO function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awareness courses are designed to introduce new emergency managers to the concepts underlying the PIO role and to build foundational knowledge needed to be full or part-time PIOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core PIO Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills needed to be full or part-time PIOs, including oral and written communications; understanding and working with the media; and basic tools and techniques to perform effectively as a PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These skills apply during proactive/advocacy times as well as crisis/emergency response; courses are intended to equip participants with these competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Audience / Intended Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: New emergency managers from State, local, tribal, territorial, and Federal emergency management agencies; and executive level roles needing PIO knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content is appropriate both for those entering PIO positions and for executives who must understand PIO responsibilities during an emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-29: Public Information Officer Awareness (Independent Study)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Information Officer Awareness Course (IS-0029) is designed to familiarize participants with the concepts underlying the PIO role and provide a basic understanding of the PIO function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery: Independent Study (IS). Course Length: 7 hours. Prerequisite guidance: participants will benefit from participating in entry-level Incident Command System training prior to taking this course.

rubrics_metrics.name: E0105: Public Information Basics (Classroom Course)
rubrics_metrics.description: To equip participants with the skills needed to be full or part-time PIOs, including oral and written communications; understanding and working with the media; and basic tools and techniques to perform effectively as a PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery: Classroom (Resident (E), Local (L), Virtual (K)). Prerequisite: IS-29. Course Length: 3 days (24 hours). Emphasizes performance in both proactive/advocacy and crisis/emergency response contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite Recommendations and Sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended and required preparatory training for the PIO courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry-level Incident Command System (ICS) training is recommended before taking IS-29. Completion of IS-29 is a prerequisite for enrolling in E0105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Length / Time Commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IS-29: 7 hours (independent study). E0105: 3 days (24 hours) classroom instruction. Time expectations should be used to plan participation and staffing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery Modes and Formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Available methods to take the courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IS-29 is offered as an Independent Study course. E0105 is offered as Resident (E), Local (L), and Virtual (K) classroom deliveries. Select format based on learner needs and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with National Emergency Management Basic Academy (NEMBA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relationship of the PIO courses to broader FEMA curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both PIO awareness courses comprise a portion of the National Emergency Management Basic Academy (NEMBA) curriculum, indicating they are foundational elements within the basic academy pathway.
